name: Chilli Chicken

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken (thigh or breast)
ingredients.householdMeasure: about 1 medium breast or 2 thighs, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Oil, for deep frying (about 8 g absorbed)
ingredients.householdMeasure: about 10 tbsp, to a depth of 2 cm in a small kadai

equipment: Small deep kadai or deep frying pan (for about 2 cm of oil)
Wok or wide, heavy pan for the sauce
Bowl for the chicken, small bowl for the sauce
Chopping board and knife; kitchen scale and measuring spoons
Kitchen paper or a plate lined with newspaper under a paper towel, to drain

steps.title: Cut the chicken
steps.text: Cut 150 g boneless chicken into 2 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: Even, same-size cubes with no bone or gristle
steps.cameraCheck: The plate of cubes on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife cutting chicken into even cubes
steps.watchOut: Pieces of different sizes: small ones turn dry while big ones stay raw inside. Keep them within about 2 cm; trim extra fat.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: In a bowl mix the chicken with 5 ml soy sauce, 0.5 g pepper, 0.5 g salt and 5 g ginger-garlic paste. Leave for 15 min.
steps.visualCue: Every piece is coated evenly in a thin brown film, with no dry patches
steps.videoShot: Hands tossing chicken cubes in the marinade
steps.watchOut: Marinating much longer than an hour with the soy sauce: the chicken turns salty and firm. Stick to 15–30 min.

steps.title: Cut the vegetables
steps.text: Cut 40 g onion into petals, 40 g capsicum into 2 cm squares, slit 2 green chillies, chop 8 g garlic and 4 g ginger, and slice the spring onion (keep whites and greens apart).
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces ready in a bowl or on a plate
steps.cameraCheck: The prepared vegetables on a plate
steps.watchOut: Pieces too small: they turn soft in the hot wok. Keep onion and capsicum about 2 cm so they stay crunchy.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: In a small bowl stir 8 ml soy sauce, 8 g red chilli sauce, 8 g ketchup, 3 ml vinegar, 1.5 g sugar and 30 ml water.
steps.visualCue: A uniform, reddish-brown sauce with the sugar dissolved
steps.watchOut: Adding it to the wok only at the last moment unmixed: sauces burn on their own. Keep it ready in the bowl before heating the wok.

steps.title: Make the batter coating
steps.text: Add 12 g cornflour, 8 g maida and 15 ml water to the marinated chicken and mix with your hand.
steps.visualCue: A thin, sticky coating that clings to each piece, like thick paint, with no loose flour
steps.cameraCheck: The coated chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Hand mixing the batter into the chicken
steps.watchOut: A thick, pasty batter or dry flour: either gives hard, floury pieces or stuck-together lumps. Add 1 tsp water if flour is dry, or a pinch of cornflour if the coating drips off.
steps.funFact: Wikipedia lists Kolkata as the place of origin of chilli chicken.

steps.title: Heat the frying oil
steps.text: Pour 150 ml oil into the kadai and heat on medium-high for 3 min.
steps.visualCue: A tiny piece of batter dropped in sinks briefly, then rises and sizzles within 2–3 seconds
steps.cameraCheck: A drop of batter sizzling in the oil
steps.videoShot: A batter drop rising and sizzling in the oil
steps.watchOut: Oil that is too cold (the coating soaks oil and falls off) or smoking hot (outside burns, inside raw). If it smokes, lower the flame and wait 1 min.

steps.title: Fry the chicken in two batches
steps.text: Lower half the pieces in one by one and fry for 3–4 min, turning once, then lift out. Repeat with the rest.
steps.visualCue: Light golden, crisp-looking pieces that float, with the bubbling slowing down
steps.cameraCheck: The golden fried chicken on the plate
steps.videoShot: Slotted spoon lifting golden chicken from the oil
steps.watchOut: Crowding the kadai: the oil cools and the pieces stick or turn pale and soggy. Fry in two batches with space between pieces. Cut one open: the meat should be white with no pink.

steps.title: Drain the chicken
steps.text: Place the pieces on kitchen paper and let them rest for 2 min.
steps.visualCue: The paper takes up a little oil and the pieces are dry on the outside
steps.videoShot: Fried chicken resting on kitchen paper
steps.watchOut: Stacking hot pieces in a covered bowl: they steam and lose crispness. Leave them open on the paper.

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Pour out the frying oil (or use a clean wok). Heat 5 g (1 tsp) oil in the wok on high for 1 min.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and a wisp of faint smoke rises
steps.cameraCheck: The hot wok with shimmering oil
steps.videoShot: Oil shimmering in a hot wok
steps.watchOut: A lukewarm wok: the vegetables stew and turn limp. Wait until the oil shimmers.

steps.title: Fry the garlic and ginger
steps.text: Add 8 g chopped garlic, 4 g ginger and the slit green chillies and stir for 15–20 sec.
steps.visualCue: A strong garlic smell and a sizzle, with the garlic still pale gold
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with garlic, ginger and chillies
steps.watchOut: Browning the garlic: it turns bitter. If it darkens fast, add the onion at once to cool the wok.

steps.title: Stir-fry the onion and capsicum
steps.text: Add 40 g onion and 40 g capsicum and stir on high for 1 min.
steps.visualCue: Onion edges turn slightly clear while the capsicum stays bright green and crisp
steps.cameraCheck: The bright, crunchy vegetables in the wok
steps.videoShot: Tossing onion and capsicum in the wok
steps.watchOut: Cooking until soft: soggy vegetables ruin the dish. Keep the flame on high and take it to the next step as soon as the colours brighten.

steps.title: Add the sauce
steps.text: Pour in the sauce mixture and stir for 20 sec.
steps.visualCue: The sauce bubbles hard and darkens slightly
steps.cameraCheck: The bubbling sauce in the wok
steps.videoShot: Sauce poured into the hot wok
steps.watchOut: Adding more water to make it saucy: the dish is meant to be dry. If it looks very watery, cook it 30 sec longer on high.

steps.title: Toss in the chicken
steps.text: Add the fried chicken and the spring onion whites and toss on high for 1–2 min.
steps.visualCue: The sauce thickens and turns glossy, coating each piece, with almost no liquid left in the wok
steps.cameraCheck: The glossy, sauce-coated chicken in the wok
steps.videoShot: Chicken tossed in the sauce in the wok
steps.watchOut: Cooking too long: the crispy coating turns soft in the sauce. Stop as soon as the sauce clings; serve straight away.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Switch off the heat, scatter the spring onion greens and serve at once.
steps.visualCue: Glossy red-brown pieces with bright green capsicum and spring onion, steaming
steps.videoShot: Spring onion sprinkled over the plate
steps.watchOut: Letting it sit in the wok: it turns soft and soggy in 10 min. Move it to a plate immediately.

reasons: about 32 g protein from lean chicken and a handful of onion and capsicum make it protein-rich, with moderate saturated fat (about 3.3 g) when made in a neutral oil. Points off for deep-frying, high sodium (about 1,230 mg from soy and chilli sauce) and cholesterol (about 190 mg). Restaurant versions use more oil, red colour, more sauce and larger plates, so the sodium and fat are higher (est.).

researchRating.basis: one of the most popular Indo-Chinese starters in India and carried by almost every major recipe site; the MyFoodStory dry version showed a 4.92 average from 50 votes in a search snippet. Points off because recipes vary a lot (egg or not, batter ratios) and the vote counts of most pages could not be read.

storage: Best eaten fresh; the coating goes soft within 30 min. Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freeze the plain fried pieces (before saucing) for about 1 month (est.); reheat in an oven or air fryer at 180°C for 6–8 min, not in a microwave, which makes it soggy.
leftoverRemix: Chilli chicken wrap. Chop the cold chicken, warm it in a pan for 2 min, and roll it in a roti with 1 tbsp mayonnaise or curd, shredded cabbage and sliced onion.
burnOff: about 6.4 km of running (450 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 9.0 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 48 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: chicken, onion and garlic, and soy sauce and vinegar are not allowed in the common vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: non-veg, onion and garlic, and grain flour.

jain.reason: chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger.

ramadan.reason: use halal chicken. Good as an iftar protein, but heavy and salty for sehri (about 1,230 mg sodium, est.).

jain.reason: contains chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger. Not appropriate to convert.

vegan.reason: chicken. (Chilli Paneer is dish 34; a tofu or soya version would be a different dish.)

sattvik.reason: the recipe uses onion, garlic and chicken.

glutenFree.reason: maida (wheat flour) in the batter and soy sauce, which usually contains wheat. See the Gluten-free variant.

dairyFree.reason: no milk, curd, butter, ghee, paneer or cream in the recipe (check the label of bottled sauces).
